description: Violations of regulatory policies, unaligned enterprise deployment, or compliance failures.
Deliberate use of generative AI or autonomous agents to develop offensive malware, automated attacks, or cyberweapons.
Compromise of backend GPU clusters, vector databases, inference endpoints, or orchestration pipelines.
Other emerging and multi-vector AI agent security incidents.
Exfiltration or compromise of API keys, authentication tokens, and service credentials by or through AI agents.
Unintended autonomous loops, unconstrained spending, resource exhaustion, or unintended destruction of production data.
Data contamination, gaming safety benchmarks, or adversarial manipulation of model evaluation leaderboards.
Breakout from Docker containers, WebAssembly sandboxes, or virtual environments by autonomous coding agents.
Vulnerabilities and unauthorized tool invocations targeting Model Context Protocol servers and agent interfaces.
Third-party untrusted data or web context hijacking an LLM agent's execution flow and instructions.
Backdoored pretrained models, poisoned datasets, compromised agent plugins, or malicious package dependencies.
Extraction of private system prompts, sensitive customer PII, intellectual property, or proprietary training corpora.
